text:
maria: heads-up — rolled the tail-latency batch controller to a 10% canary last night for a couple of noisy routes, mainly /generate-chat and /summarize.
aj: saw the canary logs, looks like /generate-chat p95 jumped from ~88ms to ~115ms in the 02:00–03:00 window.
maria: yeah that's the spike. median fine, but the tail moved. suspecting batch formation delay + kernel selection fallback.
devon: profiling from bench-bot attached a few samples — small microbatches falling back to the generic matmul kernel adds ~0.7–1.1ms per token when seq_len < 16.
aj: that aligns. when the controller tightens token_budget for a route it sometimes forces smaller microbatches; runtime chooses a different kernel path.
kelsey: could be compounded by KV cache coldness: more tokens per request during first few calls -> makes the budget hit and causes earlier microbatch flush.
maria: exact concern. We want the controller to respect tail SLOs without forcing pathological kernel choices.
devon: suggested quick mitigation — route-level override to prefer kernel X even for small batches. but that sacrifices some throughput on other shapes.
aj: alternative: make token_budget target dynamic by tier + recent batch shape histogram. If most requests have seq_len 8–12, allow slightly higher token_budget so microbatches coalesce.
kelsey: can we try a hybrid policy: keep strict budget for free tier, relaxed for paid/enterprise; and also a short warmup window for KV cache where we accept larger budgets for first N requests per session.
maria: sounds good. propose experiment config (canary -> 10% then 25%):
```
{
  "controller": "tail-latency-v2",
  "global_token_budget_ms": 100,
  "route_overrides": {
    "/generate-chat": { "token_budget_ms": 120, "tier": "auto" },
    "/summarize": { "token_budget_ms": 110 }
  },
  "tier_policies": {
    "free": { "budget_ms": 90 },
    "paid": { "budget_ms": 120, "kernel_preference": "low-latency" }
  },
  "kv_warmup_requests": 3
}
```
aj: +1 for warmup. also add a flag to prefer small-batch optimized kernel when budget/shape indicates better tail control.
devon: I'll patch a low-risk opt in the runtime: `prefer_smallbatch_kernel: conditional` keyed by route override. bench-bot will run microbench workload.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started -> tail-latency-v2 to 10% (nodes: 6) :rocket:
bench-bot: microbench results (canary 10%): /generate-chat p95 dropped to 98ms (from 115), median unchanged. KV warmup reduced first-call p95 by ~22ms.
kelsey: nice. can we push canary to 25% tomorrow and keep telemetry for kernel selection ratios + batch size histograms?
maria: yes. action items: devon -> runtime patch + bench harness, aj -> telemetry dashboard showing kernel selection by route and batch size distribution, kelsey -> prepare rollout plan and customer impact note.
aj: I'll add two charts: kernel_ratio_by_route, batch_size_histogram_5m. putting a dashboard link in #eng-runtime when ready.
devon: starting PR now, will include unit tests for fallback path.
maria: thanks — will monitor overnight and update. :eyes:
